Description: The NYU SPS Tisch Institute for Global Sport offers the Certificate in Media Management to prepare professionals for roles in managing and developing media businesses and content. This cutting-edge, graduate-level program brings together the critical business skills required to succeed in the dynamic world of media management. The NYU SPS Tisch Institute for Global Sport’s Media Management Certificate is a graduate-level program that examines the current media landscape and prepares students for roles in developing and managing media businesses and content across various sectors. The program is designed to develop the critical business skills required to succeed in the dynamic world of media management today, providing courses focused on finance, strategy, marketing, and the rapidly changing media ecosystem.

Department: Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: The Media Scoring and Production program at NYU Steinhardt prepares students for professional careers as composers and producers in film, television, interactive media, and other visual arts.

ProgramName: Media Scoring and Production MM Online
Requirements: A completed online application. Application fee. Academic transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended. Two letters of recommendation. Audition/Portfolio: Composition Portfolio: Upload a portfolio of 3-5 of your most representative scores and recordings directly to the online application. MIDI realizations are acceptable if live recordings are not available. Scores for works with recorded excerpts should be provided as one PDF file. Works for which scores are not available (e.g., electronic works) may be represented by recorded excerpts alone. Recordings of ensemble works may be submitted in audio or video format (audio preferred). All scores should clearly represent the applicant's original work. Short Composition Prompts: Please submit one example of a short composition prompt: Re-harmonize the melody and bassline of “I’ll Be Home For Christmas” (Lead Sheet is available here: https://steinhardt.nyu.edu/sites/default/files/2023-08/I%27ll%20Be%20Home%20for%20Christmas%20-%20Lead%20Sheet.pdf ) Using the melody and given bassline, create a new arrangement for a jazz quartet (piano, bass, drums, guitar, saxophone, or similar instrumentation). Use at least three of the suggested instruments in your score and recording. The arrangement must be 1-2 minutes in length. Submit a recording of your arrangement via YouTube or SoundCloud link. This recording can be a MIDI realization but must be well-produced. Submit a PDF of your score that includes piano and bass, plus three additional instruments. GRE not required.
Department: Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: The MM in Music Theory and Composition: Screen Scoring is a comprehensive two-year master’s program with instruction that balances practical training with a critical engagement of music and its relationship to visual media. Students will study with faculty and mentors who are actively involved in the industry, and they will participate in a number of professional development and networking opportunities. Through a balance of seminar and practical studio-based work, students will be prepared to work as composers, orchestrators, and music producers for film, television, games, advertising, and other forms of visual media. The program provides an immersive, project-based curriculum focused on developing the compositional, orchestrational, technological, and entrepreneurial skills needed to navigate the ever-evolving entertainment industry. Students develop an extensive portfolio of their creative work in conjunction with opportunities for live recordings of their compositions. Students also engage with the cultural, historical, and aesthetic dimensions of music for visual media, focusing on current issues and emerging practices within the field. This includes topics like: Developing compositional and orchestrational skills; Learning about music technology, including digital audio workstations and software synthesizers; Understanding the business aspects of screen scoring; Exploring the history and aesthetics of film music; Gaining experience through internships and professional opportunities.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Medical Humanities and Bioethics
Requirements: Applicants to the MA in Medical Humanities and Bioethics program must meet the general requirements for admission to GSAS. Candidates should hold a bachelor’s degree in a related field, though applicants with backgrounds in natural sciences, humanities, and social sciences are welcome. Required application materials include: a Statement of Purpose, three letters of recommendation, official transcripts from each college or university attended, and a non-refundable application fee ($85). The GRE General Test results are strongly recommended; applicants with strong academic records may request a waiver from the Director of Graduate Studies. English Language Proficiency is required for all international applicants unless they meet specific exemption criteria. Unofficial transcripts are uploaded with the application, with official transcripts required upon admission and matriculation. The Statement of Purpose should provide a clear and concise picture of academic and research interests.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science (GSAS)
Description: NYU’s MA in Medical Humanities and Bioethics offers students a flexible, interdisciplinary course of study in medicine and its social, cultural, ethical, historical, philosophical, and literary dimensions. Students can choose from a range of courses in disciplines such as bioethics, disability studies, the history of medicine, gender and sexuality studies, medical anthropology, the medical humanities, and science and technology studies. Situated in the Division of Medical Humanities in NYU Langone Health, the MA program is led by world-renowned experts in bioethics and medical humanities and offers students the opportunity to learn from leading scholars, clinicians, and researchers in the field. The MA in Medical Humanities and Bioethics prepares students for careers in medical ethics, public health, health advocacy, science writing, research, and policy. It also offers excellent preparation for further graduate study in the humanities and social sciences or for professional school in medicine, law, or public health.

Requirements: Applicants must apply to the Graduate School of Arts and Science for a certificate program. The same application, admissions standards, and deadlines that apply to the master’s and doctoral programs apply to certificates. Required application materials include: online application form, a statement of academic purpose, three letters of recommendation, official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, and an application fee. The GRE General Test is required. An English Language Proficiency requirement applies for non-native English speakers.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science (GSAS), Department of Physics
Description: The Medical Physics Certificate Program offers an immersive curriculum that delves into the foundational concepts of medical physics, encompassing radiation physics, imaging physics, and nuclear medicine. The program is designed for graduate students who seek to specialize in the rapidly evolving field of medical physics, equipping them with the theoretical knowledge and practical skills essential for a career in clinical settings, research, or industry.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Medical Radiation Dosimetry
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to graduate study at NYU Tandon School of Engineering. Please submit the following documents with your application: A resume or CV, A statement of purpose, Three (3) letters of recommendation, Official transcripts for all higher education institutions attended, Official GRE scores (if applicable, see below), Official TOEFL/IELTS/PTE Academic scores (if applicable, see below), Optional: Any other documents you wish to include. A four-year bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. A strong background in science, including a full year of college-level physics and mathematics (including calculus). Other recommended courses include anatomy and physiology, biology, and chemistry. Experience in a clinical setting is preferred, but not required. International applicants must meet additional requirements as outlined by the Office of Graduate Admissions.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Meteorology and Physical Oceanography
Requirements: Applicants must apply online to the Graduate School of Arts and Science (GSAS) and submit required materials through the online application portal. A list of general application requirements for all GSAS programs can be found on the GSAS website. In addition to the general GSAS requirements, applicants to the M.S. in Atmosphere and Ocean Science (Meteorology and Physical Oceanography) program should submit the following: A current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV); A statement of academic purpose outlining the candidate's academic interests, related experiences, and reasons for applying to the M.S. program; Three letters of recommendation; Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended; The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) general test scores are NOT required for applicants to the M.S. program. They are neither required nor considered in the review process; English language proficiency examination scores (for non-native English speakers).
Description: The MS in Mathematics program at the NYU Tandon School of Engineering offers students a flexible curriculum that allows for specialization in one of three tracks: Applied Mathematics, Scientific Computing, or Pure Mathematics. This program is suitable for students with a bachelor's degree in mathematics, engineering, or a related field who are interested in pursuing a career in industry, government, or academia, or who plan to continue their studies at the doctoral level. Our program prepares students for a diverse range of careers where strong analytical and quantitative skills are highly valued.

Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science (GSAS)
Description: The Ph.D. program in Meteorology and Physical Oceanography is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous education in the atmospheric and ocean sciences. The program emphasizes both theoretical and applied aspects of meteorology and physical oceanography, with a strong focus on research. Students will develop a deep understanding of the fundamental physical principles governing the atmosphere and oceans, and gain the skills necessary to conduct independent research in these fields. The program prepares graduates for careers in academia, government, and industry.

Requirements: Online Application, Resume/CV, Statement of Academic Purpose, Letters of Recommendation (3), Transcripts, GRE General Test, English Language Proficiency Test (if applicable), Application Fee.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science
Description: The Sackler Institute of Graduate Biomedical Sciences offers PhD training programs in several basic science disciplines. The Sackler Institute at NYU Langone Health trains future leaders in biomedical research through graduate study in our seven PhD programs, an MD/PhD Program, and a variety of postdoctoral programs. Students benefit from the mentorship of more than 450 faculty members in 30 departments at NYU Grossman School of Medicine and other NYU schools and colleges who are pursuing biomedical research, with areas of expertise that include biochemistry, cell biology, genetics, molecular pharmacology, neuroscience, microbiology, immunology, and structural biology. Our students conduct research that spans the breadth of immunology and microbiology, from basic studies of host–pathogen interactions to translational studies of human diseases. Research topics include pathogenesis and host response to viral and bacterial infection, molecular mechanisms of immune cell development, inflammation and autoimmune disease, tumor immunity, vaccine development, and immunotherapy. Our interdisciplinary program draws faculty from multiple departments at NYU Langani Health, including Microbiology, Pathology, Medicine, and Pediatrics, as well as faculty from the NYU College of Dentistry and the NYU Tandon School of Engineering.

Requirements: The online application form includes questions about your academic history, test scores, publications, and research experience. Three letters of recommendation are required. Please upload an unofficial transcript from each post-secondary institution you have attended or are currently attending. English language proficiency exams (TOEFL/IELTS/PTE) are required for all applicants who are not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, unless they received (or will receive) a bachelor’s or master’s degree from an institution where the sole language of instruction is English. The GRE General Test is not required and will not be considered.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science
Description:
Molecular and Cellular Pharmacology, part of NYU Langone’s Vilcek Institute of Graduate Biomedical Sciences, is an interdisciplinary program designed to train students for careers in the pharmacological sciences. Our faculty members work across various basic science and clinical departments and institutes to investigate all aspects of drug action, from understanding the initial molecular steps of drug binding to target identification, cellular mechanisms, and therapeutic outcomes.

The program includes coursework, laboratory rotations, seminars, and thesis research, with an emphasis on hands-on laboratory experience. Our program offers many opportunities for collaborative research, including those with scientists at NYU Langone’s Perlmutter Cancer Center, Cardiovascular Research Center, Neuroscience Institute, and Vaccine Center.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships, Tuition Waivers

ProgramName: Molecular Cell and Developmental Biology PhD
Requirements: For general admission requirements and instructions on how to apply, visit the Graduate School of Arts and Science’s (GSAS) Admissions section. All applicants must submit the online application, a statement of academic purpose, a resume or curriculum vitae (CV), transcripts from each college or university attended, and two letters of recommendation. GRE scores are optional.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science
Description: Research in Molecular, Cell and Developmental Biology addresses fundamental questions in biological processes at the molecular, cellular, and organismal levels. We study gene expression, protein structure and function, cell signaling, cell division, cell differentiation, development, and disease using a variety of model systems including bacteria, yeast, plants, flies, worms, fish, and mice, as well as cultured mammalian cells. We apply biochemical, biophysical, genetic, genomic, and imaging approaches to uncover fundamental mechanisms that control the function of cells and organisms.
ScholarshipType: Fellowship, Tuition Remission, Teaching Assistantship, Research Assistantship, Merit-based

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Motion Pictures
Description: The MFA in Film at NYU Tisch School of the Arts is a three-year graduate filmmaking program focused on developing exceptional storytellers. Our students hone their craft by making films from day one, mastering the different roles of the filmmaking process, from directing, writing, and producing to cinematography, sound, and editing. Students develop their unique voices and visions through extensive hands-on experience, rigorous coursework, and close mentorship with our award-winning faculty. Our approach is to foster a collaborative and creative environment where students experiment with different genres and forms, push boundaries, and create original works that resonate with audiences worldwide. Our alumni go on to become successful filmmakers, screenwriters, producers, cinematographers, and editors, shaping the future of cinema and storytelling.

Requirements: Complete the online application. Submit the following materials through the online application: Resume/CV, Statement of Purpose, Transcripts, Letters of Recommendation, GRE (optional), Audition (see below for details), Artistic Statement (see below for details), Additional Department-Specific Requirements (see below for details), Proof of English Language Proficiency
Department: Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: The Master of Music in Instrumental Performance is designed for highly qualified performers who wish to pursue careers as professional musicians and teachers. As a student in this program, you will focus on developing your artistic identity while cultivating the technical skills, artistry, and musicianship necessary for a successful career in today’s music world. You will take private lessons and participate in large and small ensembles and chamber music. You will also have opportunities to participate in master classes with renowned guest artists and faculty members, and to perform in various recitals, concerts, and special events throughout the year. You will develop your professional network in New York City and beyond, and gain the skills necessary to pursue your musical career. Your curriculum will also include academic studies in music theory, history, and pedagogy, enabling you to become a well-rounded musician and educator.

Requirements: The application requires the following: Statement of Purpose, Resume, 3 Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts, Proof of English Language Proficiency (for international applicants), and an Application Fee. Supplemental materials required include an Audition, Repertoire List, and a Writing Sample (a research paper from a graduate-level course, thesis chapter, or professional article, minimum 10 pages, maximum 25 pages). The GRE General Test is not required.
Department: Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: The Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) in Music Performance at NYU Steinhardt is designed to prepare musician-scholars for careers in performance and/or teaching at the university level. Our unique curriculum combines high-level performance training with rigorous academic study in areas such as performance studies, music history, and music theory. You will complete your degree with a final dissertation that may include a written document, a lecture recital, or a combination of both. You’ll also perform a series of required recitals throughout your time in the program. You'll learn to become a well-rounded musician-scholar through: Intensive one-on-one instruction with our distinguished performance faculty; Advanced studies in music history, theory, and performance studies; Participation in NYU’s world-class performance ensembles; Opportunities for advanced study in related fields, such as music education, music technology, and performing arts administration; Engage with the vibrant musical life of New York City through master classes, concerts, and collaborations with leading artists and institutions.
CostPerCredit: 2127 per point (before completing 45 points beyond master's degree); 1064 per point (after completing 45 points beyond master's degree)

Requirements: The Music Business Fundamentals online certificate application includes a short questionnaire about your academic background and professional experience, an unofficial transcript, and a short essay (250–500 words).
Description: The Music Business Fundamentals Certificate Online provides students with an overview of the music industry from a business perspective. Through engaging video lectures, dynamic discussions, and written assignments, students will gain insight into the structures, processes, and essential practices of the contemporary music business. This certificate focuses on the fundamentals of the industry, including music publishing and licensing, copyrights, distribution, record labels, and how artists are managed and promoted. Students will explore traditional and modern business models, learning how the internet and new technologies have shaped the industry and are changing the way music is created, marketed, and consumed.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Music Industry
Requirements: All applicants for the Music Business Master of Arts program must apply through the NYU Steinhardt Graduate Admissions Application. Here are the materials you'll need to prepare: Online Application, Application Fee, Transcripts, Statement of Purpose, Resume or CV, Letters of Recommendation (Two letters of recommendation are required.), Standardized Tests (GRE General Test: Not required. English Language Proficiency Test: Required for international applicants who do not meet specific criteria.), Video Audition/Portfolio (Optional: While not required, you may submit a short video of you performing or discussing music, or a portfolio of your creative work.), Interview (Optional: We may ask you to interview in-person or online with members of our faculty. We will contact you directly if an interview is requested.)
Department: NYU Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: Prepare for a dynamic career in the evolving music industry with our MA in Music Business. Ranked among the top music business programs in the world, we offer a rigorous, interdisciplinary curriculum, unmatched internship opportunities, and unparalleled access to the global music industry in the heart of New York City. Students gain the knowledge and skills for leadership roles across all sectors of the music industry. You'll learn from world-renowned faculty and industry leaders through real-world projects, case studies, guest speakers, and hands-on experiences. Graduates work in all areas of the industry, including record companies, music publishers, artist management firms, concert promotion companies, music technology firms, media and entertainment companies, and as entrepreneurs and independent artists. Through this program, you will also learn about: Music business history and evolution; The economics and legal aspects of the music business; Current trends, strategies, and challenges in the global music industry; Digital distribution, marketing, and monetization strategies; Artist management, concert promotion, and live entertainment; Entrepreneurship, innovation, and leadership in music; Data analytics and research methods for decision-making; International music markets and global business practices; Practical skills through internships and industry projects.

Requirements:
All applicants for graduate programs at NYU Steinhardt must apply through the Steinhardt Graduate Admissions Application. When applying, be sure to upload the following items:
Unofficial transcripts from all colleges/universities you have attended are required for the application review. If admitted, official transcripts will be required.
Two letters of recommendation are required.
In one to two pages, describe your academic and professional qualifications, interests, and objectives related to the program. Indicate how our faculty and resources would assist you in achieving your goals. For students applying to both the Music Business MA and the JD/MA program, please be sure to address your interest in both degrees.
A résumé or curriculum vitae (CV) is required. Please include all relevant academic and work experience.
GRE scores are not required for this program. International students who are required to submit TOEFL/IELTS/PTE/Duolingo scores should refer to English Language Proficiency Testing Requirements.
A non-refundable application fee of $85.00 is required.
Department: NYU Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: The MA in Music Business program at NYU Steinhardt provides students with a comprehensive curriculum in areas such as record company operations, music publishing, artist management, digital distribution, marketing, and entrepreneurship. You'll gain valuable experience through internships, special projects, and opportunities to network with professionals in New York City and beyond. Graduates of our program become leaders in record companies, music publishing companies, artist management firms, concert promotion companies, music products firms, and many new ventures. Our faculty members are leading executives in the music industry who integrate theory and practice throughout the curriculum. Our alumni are working in virtually every sector of the music industry in the US and around the world. The MA in Music Business is offered both on campus and online. The online program is designed for working professionals who wish to advance their careers in the global music industry.
ScholarshipType: Endowed scholarships, Assistantships, Fellowships, Veterans Benefits (Yellow Ribbon Program)

Requirements: The MA in Music Education program requires the following: Online Application, Application Fee, Academic Transcripts, Two Letters of Recommendation, Statement of Purpose: Your statement of purpose should be 2-3 pages, double-spaced. Please describe your professional goals, any significant teaching, leadership, or performance experiences, and how the MA in Music Education program will help you achieve your goals. Your statement should clearly indicate whether you are applying for the Initial Certification (for students who do not have prior teaching certification) or Professional Certification (for students who already hold teaching certification) path. GRE General Test: The GRE General Test is optional for Fall 2024 applicants to the Music Education MA. If you believe your GRE scores strengthen your application, you may submit them. If you do not submit GRE scores, your application will be reviewed without them. There is no minimum score requirement, and successful applicants typically have a balance of strong verbal, quantitative, and analytical writing scores. NYU Steinhardt's GRE code is 2599. English Language Proficiency, Resume/CV: Please include all work experience, particularly any teaching and/or performing experience. Audition: All applicants are required to complete an audition. If you reside within 150 miles of New York City, you must complete an in-person audition. If you reside beyond 150 miles of New York City, you may submit a video audition via the online application. In-person Audition Requirements (select your primary instrument/voice for specific repertoire) Brass Composition Guitar (Classical, Jazz) Percussion Piano (Classical, Jazz) Strings (Classical, Jazz) Voice (Classical, Jazz) Woodwinds Video Audition Requirements (same repertoire requirements as in-person) New York State Initial or Professional Teaching Certification: If you are applying for the Professional Certification path and already hold teaching certification, please upload a copy of your New York State Initial or Professional teaching certification. If you are applying for the Initial Certification path, this document is not required.
Department: NYU Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: The Master of Arts (MA) in Music Education program will prepare you to be an innovative music educator in a range of settings. As a graduate student, you'll choose a focus in one of the following areas to suit your interests and career goals: Instrumental, Vocal, and General Music Teaching; Music and the Creative Technologies; Music Education and Special Education; or Music Therapy. Our program is known for its strong faculty, who are leaders in their fields, and for its diverse student body. You'll have opportunities to engage in research, creative projects, and performances, and to collaborate with faculty and peers on various initiatives. Our alumni are successful practitioners, scholars, and leaders in music education worldwide.

Requirements: All applicants to graduate programs in Music must submit the following materials: Online Application, Application Fee, Academic Transcripts, Two letters of recommendation from individuals qualified to assess your academic potential, scholarly ability, and/or professional promise, A current resume or CV describing your academic, professional, and performance experience, A 1-2 page essay describing your academic and professional objectives and how they align with your interest in your program of study at NYU Steinhardt. Standardized Tests: The GRE General Test is not required for applicants to any graduate program in Music at NYU Steinhardt. English Language Proficiency Test (if applicable). For Music Education (MM, MM w/ Cert, PhD, Advanced Cert): Applicants must submit a separate artistic statement of no more than 500 words and schedule a brief interview with a faculty member via Zoom. This interview is not an audition.
Department: Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: The Music Education MM with Certification program at NYU Steinhardt is for students seeking a master’s degree and initial or professional New York State teacher certification. This program is for students who have completed an undergraduate degree and are seeking teacher certification in music education, or for professional teachers who already have initial certification and are seeking a master’s degree and professional certification. This program combines advanced academic study in music education with required coursework and field experiences that prepare you to become a certified music educator. Upon successful completion of the program, you will be recommended for initial or professional certification.
Accredidation: Registered by the New York State Education Department (NYSED); Accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM)

Requirements: Official transcripts from each post-secondary institution you have attended. Three letters of recommendation. A statement of purpose. A professional resume or curriculum vitae. GRE scores are optional for all master's and PhD programs for spring 2024, fall 2024, spring 2025, and fall 2025 entry terms. Applicants may choose to submit GRE scores if they believe the scores will strengthen their application. A writing sample may be required for some programs. Portfolios and Auditions may be required for some programs.
Department: NYU Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: The PhD in Music Education provides an intensive program of study in research and scholarship, preparing students for careers as university professors and researchers. In this program, students develop a deep understanding of philosophical, historical, psychological, and sociological aspects of music teaching and learning. Graduates become leaders in the field, making significant contributions to music education scholarship and practice. Our doctoral program offers a concentration in research within a broad range of music education topics. Our faculty have expertise in areas such as music performance, music teacher education, urban music education, popular music, music technology, early childhood music, social justice, psychology of music, arts and humanities, music history, and ethnomusicology. Students pursue coursework in areas of their interest related to their dissertation research.

ProgramName: Music Education PhD with Music Therapy Emphasis
Requirements: Application Requirements: Online Application, Application Fee, Academic Transcripts, GRE Scores: GRE scores are not required. Letters of Recommendation: Three letters of recommendation are required. Statement of Purpose: Required. A statement of purpose, approximately 500 words, indicating your professional goals and interest in the program. Resume/CV: Required. Submit a resume or curriculum vitae listing your education, experience, honors, and other qualifications. Writing Sample: Required. Submit a writing sample (e.g., a published article, research paper, or master's thesis chapter) that demonstrates your ability to review the literature, formulate a research problem, and discuss findings. Additional Requirements for All Music Applicants: Academic History and Coursework: For all music applicants, please provide a comprehensive listing of all music-related courses in which you have been enrolled, including institutions, course titles, academic credits, and grades. Audition: An audition is not required for applicants to the PhD in Music Education, Music Therapy Specialization.
Department: NYU Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: Our PhD in Music Education, with a specialization in Music Therapy, is designed for experienced music therapists who hold a master’s degree and wish to pursue advanced study and research in music therapy. This specialization aims to develop leaders in research, higher education, and clinical practice, fostering critical inquiry and the generation of new knowledge in the field. You’ll gain the research competencies necessary to contribute to the body of knowledge in music therapy, explore advanced clinical topics, and prepare for leadership roles in academic or professional settings. The curriculum integrates advanced coursework in music education research methods, music therapy theory and practice, and opportunities for independent research culminating in a dissertation. Our faculty are recognized experts in their respective fields, providing mentorship and guidance throughout your doctoral journey.

Requirements: All applicants must submit the following materials: Resume or CV, Statement of Purpose, Three letters of recommendation, Academic transcripts, English Language Proficiency Exam (if applicable). GRE is not required. A Music Technology portfolio is optional.
Department: NYU Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: The Steinhardt Master of Music in Music Technology program trains musicians and media artists to work at an advanced level in the rapidly changing fields of music technology, production, and sonic arts. The MM in Music Technology can be completed on a full-time or part-time basis. Full-time students typically finish the program in two years, while part-time students can take up to five years. The program prepares students to become leaders in various careers, including audio engineering, music production, sound design, new media, scoring for film and games, and music business. Our curriculum balances theoretical coursework with hands-on practice, empowering students to develop a deep understanding of audio engineering, music production, sound synthesis, interactive media, and other cutting-edge technologies. Students learn to use industry-standard software and hardware, gaining practical experience that prepares them for success in diverse fields. Through our program, you'll develop your artistic vision, technical expertise, and critical thinking skills, enabling you to push the boundaries of music and sound.

Requirements: Our application includes a form, current resume or CV, personal statement, transcripts, and application fee. Interviews are optional and scheduled after the application is submitted. International students should apply early to allow for additional processing time.
Department: NYU Tisch School of the Arts
Description: The Online Music Entrepreneurship Certificate offers a structured pathway for students to delve into the rapidly evolving landscape of the music industry. Designed for aspiring music professionals, artists, managers, and entrepreneurs, this program provides a comprehensive understanding of business strategies, digital technologies, and legal frameworks essential for success in today’s music ecosystem. Through a blend of theoretical knowledge and practical application, students will gain the skills and insights needed to navigate challenges, identify opportunities, and innovate within the dynamic world of music.

ProgramName: Music Rights Administration and Licensing Certificate Online
Requirements: The Music Rights Administration and Licensing Certificate is open to qualified applicants. No prior knowledge of music business or music theory is required. Students apply online and will be notified of their admissions status approximately one to two weeks following the submission of their application. Rolling Admissions means that students are admitted on an ongoing basis throughout the year. It's never too late to apply! Application Requirements: A brief (300-500 words) personal statement outlining why you are interested in pursuing this particular certificate, how you hope it will help you achieve your professional goals, and what you will bring to the program. Upload a current resume or C.V. Submit unofficial transcripts from all prior higher education institutions. There is a non-refundable $75 application fee that must be submitted with your application.
Description: The Music Rights Administration and Licensing Certificate Online is designed to give you an overview of the legal and business aspects of music licensing and copyright. The program is specifically structured to offer working professionals and recent college graduates a broad understanding of the music business, with a specific focus on administration, rights, and licensing. Throughout the program, you will gain the knowledge and skills necessary to navigate the complexities of music rights, including copyright, publishing, synchronization, and master use licensing. You will learn about the various types of licenses, their associated fees, and the negotiation process. Additionally, you will explore the roles of performing rights organizations (PROs), collection societies, and other industry players. Upon completion, you will have a comprehensive understanding of the music rights landscape and be equipped to pursue careers in music publishing, music supervision, and licensing.

Requirements: All applicants for admission to graduate study at NYU Steinhardt must submit the following materials electronically: Application, Application fee, Academic transcripts, Two letters of recommendation from faculty or employers who can speak to your academic and professional qualifications, a one- to two-page Statement of Purpose addressing your professional goals, experiences, and interest in our program, and a Resume/CV. The Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) are not required for admission to this program. Applicants are required to submit proof of English language proficiency if they did not complete their entire undergraduate degree (or master's degree) at an institution where the sole language of instruction was English. Music Therapy (MA) applicants must demonstrate sufficient music proficiency by submitting an audition via a recorded video or by a live in-person audition. Competitive applicants will be invited for an interview in February or March following the application deadline.
Department: NYU Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: As one of the world's most renowned and comprehensive programs, the MA in Music Therapy at NYU Steinhardt provides you with the skills, knowledge, and experience needed to become a board-certified music therapist. Our curriculum emphasizes clinical practice, research, and theory, preparing you to work with diverse populations in various settings. You will gain a deep understanding of music therapy principles, techniques, and ethical considerations, developing your abilities to assess, plan, implement, and evaluate music therapy interventions effectively.
Accredidation: Our program is approved by the American Music Therapy Association (AMTA). Graduates of the MA in Music Therapy program are eligible to sit for the board certification examination administered by the Certification Board for Music Therapists (CBMT). Successful completion of this examination leads to the credential MT-BC (Music Therapist - Board Certified), which is required for professional practice in most settings.

ProgramName: Music Therapy MM with Undergraduate Equivalency
Requirements: To apply for the Master of Arts in Music Therapy program, please submit the following via the Steinhardt Graduate Application: Application, Application Fee, Transcripts, Recommendations (two letters), Statement of Purpose, Resume/CV, Audition, Interview, GRE General Test (Not required), TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo English Test (Required for applicants who do not meet the waiver criteria).
Department: NYU Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development

Requirements: Admission to the M.M. program in Musicology is for the fall semester only. Applicants are expected to have a strong undergraduate record and adequate preparation in music history. The GRE is not required. Required Application Materials: Statement of Purpose, Three Letters of Recommendation, Academic Transcripts, Writing Sample, Curriculum Vitae/Resume. Optional: GRE Scores (General and/or Subject Test).
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science
Description: At NYU Steinhardt, we offer master of music (MM) and doctor of philosophy (PhD) degrees in Musicology, with concentrations in Historical Musicology and Ethnomusicology. As a student in our program, you will develop expertise in the study of music through historical, cultural, and ethnographic methodologies. Our faculty specialize in a wide array of musical traditions and periods, including Western art music (medieval to present), African diasporic music, African music, Black music, Asian music, popular music, and film music. Our master's and doctoral programs provide a strong foundation for a variety of career paths in academia, arts administration, performance, and other fields that require a rigorous intellectual approach to music.

Requirements: Applicants must submit an online application, transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a statement of academic purpose, a resume/CV, and an application fee. Additionally, a writing sample, preferably a scholarly paper (20-25 pages), should be uploaded. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) general test is not required for applicants to the PhD program in Music.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science
ScholarshipAmount: A fellowship including a $32,000/year stipend, tuition waiver, and health insurance subsidy.

Requirements: All applicants to the Graduate School of Arts and Science (GSAS) are required to submit a completed online application, a statement of academic purpose, a resume or curriculum vitae (CV), and unofficial transcripts from each college or university attended. Some programs may have additional application requirements. Program Specific Requirements for Philosophy: GRE Scores: Not required. Writing Sample: Required, 10-20 pages. Letters of Recommendation: Three required. Transcripts: Unofficial transcripts are required for the application. Official transcripts are required upon admission.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science
Description: The Philosophy Department does not offer a terminal MA program. However, students who have successfully completed one year of the PhD program may apply to receive an MA from NYU. This MA is not a prerequisite for the PhD program, nor does it guarantee admission to the PhD program. For more information, please refer to the PhD Admissions section.

Requirements: All applicants must apply online through the GSAS Application. You may apply for admission for fall only. The deadline for receipt of all application materials is December 15. The Department does not admit students for Spring semester. Applications must include: Application Fee, Statement of Purpose, Writing Sample (not to exceed 5,000 words, including footnotes), Three Letters of Recommendation, All previous post-secondary transcripts, Resume/CV. GRE Scores are optional. Applicants for admission to the Philosophy PhD program who are not native speakers of English must present evidence of their proficiency in English by taking the TOEFL or IELTS examination.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science
Description: The NYU Philosophy Department offers a Ph.D. program designed to provide students with a broad and deep education in philosophy. Our program is recognized for its excellence in both core areas of philosophy and emerging fields, and for the strength of its faculty across a wide range of specialties. The Ph.D. program aims to train students to be excellent philosophers and successful academics. It typically takes five years of coursework and dissertation writing to complete the degree. Our rigorous curriculum, close faculty mentorship, and vibrant intellectual community prepare students for successful careers in academia and beyond. Students complete coursework in various areas of philosophy, including history of philosophy, metaphysics, epistemology, ethics, political philosophy, philosophy of mind, and logic. They are expected to develop strong research skills, culminating in the writing and defense of a doctoral dissertation. While students are not required to select a specific concentration or area of specialization upon admission, they are encouraged to explore their interests through seminars, research, and collaboration with faculty.
ScholarshipType: Fellowship (includes tuition remission, stipend, and health insurance coverage)

Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Specific coursework is required and must be completed prior to matriculation. The admissions committee looks for applicants who have achieved strong grades, particularly in their science coursework. Additional Application Requirements for All Applicants: Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended; Two letters of recommendation (one from a science professor and one from a licensed physical therapist); A personal statement explaining your career goals and interest in physical therapy. Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required for applicants for Fall 2024. For subsequent application cycles, GRE scores may be required. Any updates will be posted on the program website. International applicants must submit official TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores if their native language is not English and they have not completed a bachelor’s or master’s degree in an institution where the sole language of instruction is English.
Department: NYU Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: Prepare for a rewarding career helping people restore and improve movement with our Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) program. At NYU Steinhardt, you’ll learn evidence-based skills to provide ethical, client-centered care. Become a leader in physical therapy practice, research, and education. You’ll be prepared for careers in hospitals, rehabilitation centers, private practices, and community clinics. As a student in our Doctor of Physical Therapy program, you’ll be trained to work with patients across the lifespan in a variety of settings. Through courses, hands-on clinical experiences, and research opportunities, you will learn to: Conduct comprehensive evaluations and assessments of patients. Develop and implement individualized treatment plans. Promote health and wellness through education and preventative strategies. Collaborate with other healthcare professionals to optimize patient outcomes. Engage in scholarly inquiry and contribute to the advancement of physical therapy.
Accredidation: The Doctor of Physical Therapy Program at New York University is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE), 3030 Potomac Ave., Suite 100, Alexandria, Virginia 22305-3085; telephone: 703-706-3245; email: accreditation@apta.org; website: http://www.capteonline.org. If needing to contact the program/institution directly, please call 212-998-9310 or email pt.steinhardt@nyu.edu.

Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School of Arts and Science and have a Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) degree (or equivalent). In addition, applicants must submit the following: Transcripts from each college or university attended. A current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV). A statement of purpose. Three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required for admission to this program. Applicants with international degrees must demonstrate English proficiency.
Department: NYU Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Research Physical Therapy is for physical therapists who want to advance the evidence-base of physical therapy practice through research. The curriculum focuses on developing the critical thinking, research, and scholarship skills required to conduct rigorous and impactful clinical and translational research. Students gain knowledge in specific areas of inquiry related to physical therapy, including movement science, neuroscience, rehabilitation science, and health services research. Graduates are prepared for careers as independent researchers and academics in university settings, research institutes, and clinical research centers.

Requirements: Applicants are generally required to follow the application requirements set by the GSAS. Most importantly, the program is looking for a Statement of Purpose, three letters of recommendation, and transcripts from all previous universities attended. While the GSAS does not require the GRE General Test, applicants are strongly recommended to take it, as the application may be stronger with a high score. The GRE Physics Subject Test is highly encouraged but not required. An academic writing sample is asked for, if available, and can be submitted to admissions@physics.nyu.edu. All applicants are required to submit transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, and most are required to submit three letters of recommendation. All recommendation letters must be submitted online directly through the application system. Applicants must demonstrate proficiency in English unless they meet exemption criteria. A resume or CV can be a helpful supplement to the application.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science
Description:
The M.S. in Physics program provides a solid foundation in the core areas of physics while also allowing for some specialization. Students pursuing the M.S. degree at NYU typically do so for one of two reasons: either to strengthen their background in physics before applying to a Ph.D. program, or to acquire the knowledge base for a career in industry. The program can be completed with or without a thesis option.

M.S. students pursuing the non-thesis option complete a total of 32 points, or eight graduate courses. These courses include two required courses (General Physics I and II) and six elective courses. Electives can be taken from the range of graduate courses offered by the Department of Physics, in topics such as classical mechanics, quantum mechanics, electrodynamics, statistical mechanics, and more specialized areas like astrophysics, condensed matter physics, and particle physics.

M.S. students pursuing the thesis option also complete 32 points, which includes six graduate courses (24 points) and an M.S. thesis (8 points). The thesis involves original research conducted under the supervision of a faculty member and culminates in a written thesis and oral defense. The thesis option provides valuable research experience, often leading to publications, and is particularly beneficial for students considering doctoral studies.

Both options offer flexibility in course selection, allowing students to tailor their academic path to their interests and career goals. Students have access to state-of-the-art research facilities and opportunities to collaborate with leading faculty members on cutting-edge research projects.

Requirements: The deadline for fall applications is December 15. The Department of Physics only accepts applications for fall admission. To apply, you should complete a brief online application, including your transcripts, a list of courses taken, and a curriculum vitae (CV). You will also be asked to provide a statement of purpose outlining your research interests and career goals. We also require three letters of recommendation from faculty members who know you well and can comment on your academic and research abilities. All application materials, including transcripts, letters, and scores, should be sent to the NYU GSAS Admissions Office. GRE General Test and GRE Physics Subject Test scores are not required for admission to the Physics PhD program.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science
Description: The Ph.D. program in Physics is designed for students seeking to conduct original research and contribute to the scientific community. The program offers a rigorous curriculum covering foundational aspects of physics as well as advanced topics in various subfields. Students work closely with faculty mentors on cutting-edge research projects, leading to the development of a dissertation based on original scholarly work. Graduates are prepared for careers in academia, industrial research, government laboratories, and other science-related fields.
ScholarshipPercentage: 100% (of tuition, registration fees, and health insurance)

Requirements: Required Application Materials: Statement of Purpose, Resume or CV, Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts, English Language Proficiency (if applicable). Program-Specific Requirements: Audition (Recorded Submission Required): All applicants for the Popular Music Pedagogy MA Online program are required to submit an audition via recorded video submission. This should demonstrate your ability to teach in a popular music setting. The submission should be no longer than 15 minutes and include: A performance of two contrasting popular music pieces (e.g., different styles, tempos, or instrumentation). The performance can be solo, with accompaniment, or with a band. A short (3-5 minute) video demonstrating your teaching philosophy or approach in a popular music context (e.g., teaching a skill, discussing curriculum, etc.). Please provide context for your submission (e.g., a brief written description of the pieces, teaching demonstration, and rationale). Academic Writing Sample: Applicants must submit an academic writing sample, such as an excerpt from a research paper, an essay, or a critical review, demonstrating their ability to write clearly and analytically on a topic relevant to popular music or music education. The sample should be no longer than 10 pages.
Description: Our online option for the MA in Music Education with a Concentration in Popular Music Pedagogy offers working professionals a flexible, part-time path to advanced study. You’ll engage in a comprehensive curriculum covering popular music history, pedagogy, technology, and performance, preparing you to lead and innovate in various educational and community settings. Through a blend of synchronous and asynchronous learning activities, you’ll collaborate with faculty and peers, deepen your understanding of diverse musical genres, and develop practical skills to effectively teach popular music. This program is designed for current and aspiring music educators who want to expand their expertise in popular music and contribute to its growing presence in educational curricula.
ScholarshipType: MacCracken Fellowships, Dean's Awards, Departmental Aid, External Fellowships, Federal Work-Study, Loans

ProgramName: Master of Science in Prevention Science and Community Health
Requirements: Applicants to all MS programs must submit the following materials directly to SOPHAS, the centralized application service for schools and programs of public health: Online Application, Resume/CV, Statement of Purpose, Two Letters of Recommendation, Official Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, GRE General Test (waived for all applicants to MS programs for the 2024-2025 academic year), English Language Proficiency (if applicable), Application Fee.
Department: NYU School of Global Public Health
Description: The MS in Prevention Science and Community Health is an interdisciplinary program designed to train future public health leaders and researchers who will develop, implement, and evaluate evidence-based interventions to improve health and health equity within communities. The program addresses the increasing demand for professionals skilled in understanding and addressing complex public health issues through a prevention science lens. Students will gain expertise in theoretical frameworks, research methodologies, and practical skills necessary to translate scientific discoveries into effective community-based programs and policies. Graduates will be prepared to work in a variety of settings, including government agencies, non-profit organizations, research institutions, and academic settings, making significant contributions to public health.

ProgramName: Prevention Science and Community Health PhD
Requirements: Online Application, Application Fee, Transcripts, 3 Letters of Recommendation, Statement of Purpose, Resume or CV, GRE General Test, and English Language Testing (TOEFL/IELTS/PTE required for international applicants unless exempt). A writing sample may be submitted as an optional item.
Department: NYU School of Global Public Health
Description:
Our PhD in Public Health, Prevention Science & Community Health (PSCH) program trains research scientists to develop and evaluate interventions to prevent disease and promote health in community, clinical, and policy settings.
As a student in the PSCH PhD program, you will develop:
*   An understanding of the etiology and course of health-related behaviors and conditions using both qualitative and quantitative methods.
*   Expertise in the design, implementation, and evaluation of evidence-based interventions to improve health outcomes, reduce health disparities, and promote health equity.
*   The ability to disseminate research findings effectively to scientific and lay audiences.
Graduates of our PhD in Public Health, Prevention Science & Community Health program pursue careers in academia, government, and non-profit organizations, as well as positions in private industry and healthcare.

ProgramName: Product Design MS in Cosmetics and Consumer Goods
Requirements: The following materials are required for all NYU Tandon School of Engineering graduate applicants: Online Application, Application Fee, Transcripts, Letters of Recommendation (Two letters of recommendation are required for all graduate applications. Three letters of recommendation are accepted. These must be submitted electronically through the application system by your recommenders.), Statement of Purpose (A statement of purpose is required for all graduate applications.), Resume/CV (A resume or curriculum vitae (CV) is required for all graduate applications.), GRE Scores (GRE scores are not required for graduate admissions for most programs at NYU Tandon School of Engineering, including the Product Design MS in Cosmetics and Consumer Goods program. If you have taken the GRE, you may submit your scores for consideration, but it is not mandatory.), English Language Proficiency (Applicants whose native language is not English and who have not received a degree from an institution where the sole language of instruction is English must demonstrate English proficiency through one of the following exams: TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo English Test, or PTE Academic.). All applicants must meet the general requirements for graduate admission at NYU Tandon School of Engineering. There are no specific additional departmental requirements for the MS in Product Design (Cosmetics and Consumer Goods) beyond the general graduate admissions requirements of the Tandon School of Engineering.
Description: Translational Surface Engineering (TSE) is a new, interdisciplinary Master of Science (MS) program that aims to equip engineers and scientists with the knowledge and skills required to solve critical challenges in developing advanced materials and devices. This is a unique program because it aims to provide students with a holistic understanding of surface engineering, including surface characterization, modification, and functionalization techniques, as well as their applications in various fields. The program focuses on the practical application of surface engineering principles to real-world problems in sectors such as biomedical, aerospace, automotive, energy, and consumer products. Students will gain expertise in areas like nanotechnology, biomaterials, coatings, and advanced manufacturing processes, preparing them for careers in research and development, product design, and process optimization. Through a combination of theoretical coursework, hands-on laboratory experience, and industry-sponsored projects, students will learn to design, synthesize, and characterize novel surface materials, analyze their performance, and translate their findings into innovative solutions. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and interdisciplinary collaboration, fostering a new generation of engineers who can bridge the gap between scientific discovery and technological innovation.

ProgramName: Product Design MS in Pharmaceutical and Biopharmaceutical
Requirements: Online Application, Application Fee, Academic Transcripts, Statement of Purpose, Resume/CV, Two Letters of Recommendation, GRE Scores (Optional for Fall 2024 and Spring 2025, recommended for applicants without an undergraduate engineering degree), English Language Proficiency (if applicable).

Admission to the Program Evaluation Advanced Certificate is highly selective. Students admitted to the certificate program typically have: A strong academic record with at least a 3.0 GPA; At least two years of full-time professional or other relevant experience for the online program. Students in any graduate degree program at NYU or any other institution, current students in the Steinhardt MS Program in Applied Psychology, or applicants with a master's degree (or higher) are also eligible to apply. Students who have previously completed graduate-level coursework related to program evaluation may be able to transfer up to 6 credits towards the certificate requirements. Please reach out to your academic advisor to determine eligibility. Required Application Materials: Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended, Letters of Recommendation (Two required), CV or Resume, Statement of Purpose, Application Fee, GRE General Test or LSAT or GMAT (not required for NYU Steinhardt graduate students), English Language Proficiency Test (if applicable).
Description: The NYU Wagner Evaluation Certificate provides students with the critical skills needed to design, implement, and manage effective evaluation strategies. Designed for working professionals, this certificate offers flexible course schedules and can be completed in one year or less. Students acquire essential evaluation skills including how to frame an evaluable program, identify program theories of change, select appropriate evaluation designs, implement mixed methods, analyze data, and communicate findings to various audiences. Students who complete the certificate will be prepared to take on evaluation roles in a variety of public, nonprofit, and private sector organizations. Students who complete the Evaluation Certificate will be able to: Frame an evaluable program; Identify appropriate theories of change; Select appropriate evaluation designs; Conduct mixed methods evaluations; Analyze qualitative and quantitative data; Communicate findings to various audiences.

ProgramName: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner Certificate
Requirements: Prerequisites for Admission: A master of science degree in nursing (MSN) or a doctor of nursing practice degree (DNP) from an accredited institution. (Post-baccalaureate DNP students are not eligible to apply for advanced certificates.) Current, unencumbered registered nurse (RN) license in the United States. Current, unencumbered advanced practice registered nurse (APRN) license in the United States in the specialty area in which the applicant is currently practicing, if applicable. National board certification as an advanced practice registered nurse (APRN) in the specialty area in which the applicant is currently practicing, if applicable. Minimum 3.0 GPA from prior master's or doctoral nursing program. Evidence of completion of graduate-level coursework in advanced pathophysiology, advanced pharmacology, and advanced health assessment. For PMHNP, prior graduate-level coursework in foundational primary care (e.g., adult, family) may also be required. Evidence of current clinical practice as an APRN in the specialty area for which you are seeking an advanced certificate or documented evidence of graduate-level clinical practice. PMHNP: Current, unencumbered APRN license in the US, and national certification as a Family, Adult, or Adult-Gerontology Nurse Practitioner, Clinical Nurse Specialist, or Certified Nurse Midwife (CNM). Additionally, applicants for the PMHNP Advanced Certificate program must submit evidence of a minimum of 500 supervised clinical hours (post-graduation from a master's or doctoral program) as an APRN and a copy of the supervising preceptor’s CV/resume along with an employment verification letter. Application Checklist: The following items are required for your application to be reviewed. Submit all materials directly through the online application portal unless otherwise specified. Online Application, Application Fee, Official Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, Current Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume, Statement of Professional Goals (approximately 500-750 words), Proof of valid, unencumbered RN License (New York State preferred, but not required for admission), Proof of valid, unencumbered APRN License and national board certification in your current advanced practice specialty, if applicable. Three Letters of Recommendation (at least one from a former faculty member and one from a current supervisor who can speak to your clinical aptitude), PMHNP Advanced Certificate applicants only: Preceptor CV/Resume, Employment Verification Letter, and Documented Evidence of 500 Supervised Clinical Hours.
Department: NYU Rory Meyers College of Nursing
Description: The Advanced Certificate for Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) program prepares registered nurses for advanced practice roles focused on providing comprehensive mental healthcare to individuals, families, and communities across the lifespan. Building on a foundation of advanced nursing theory, research, and evidence-based practice, the program emphasizes critical thinking, clinical reasoning, and therapeutic interventions to promote mental health and prevent mental illness. Graduates are equipped to assess, diagnose, treat, and manage a wide range of psychiatric conditions, as well as provide psychoeducation, counseling, and collaboration with interdisciplinary teams. The curriculum integrates didactic coursework with extensive supervised clinical experiences, ensuring proficiency in psychopharmacology, psychotherapy, and cultural competence.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Psychology: Applied Behaviour Analysis
Requirements: Applicants apply through the GSAS online application system. The application consists of the following: Application form, Application fee, Statement of Academic Purpose, Three (3) letters of recommendation, Resume or curriculum vitae, Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, Official GRE general test scores are NOT required for applicants to the M.S. in Psychology in Applied Behavior Analysis program. TOEFL/IELTS for international students (if applicable). The M.S. in Psychology in Applied Behavior Analysis program does not accept applications for spring admission. The M.S. in Psychology in Applied Behavior Analysis program requires applicants to have an undergraduate degree in Psychology or a related field with at least 12 credits in Psychology coursework, including a course in Statistics and a course in Research Methods. Additionally, applicants must have maintained a minimum overall GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) and a minimum GPA of 3.0 in Psychology coursework.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science
Description: The MS in Applied Behavior Analysis program at NYU Steinhardt provides professional and academic training for individuals interested in the theoretical and practical application of the principles of behavior. You will gain a strong foundation in behavioral principles and concepts and learn how to apply these principles to address socially significant behaviors, particularly in individuals with developmental disabilities. You'll gain expertise in designing, implementing, and evaluating behavioral interventions, conducting functional behavior assessments, and supervising others. This program prepares you to become a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA), a globally recognized certification for professionals in applied behavior analysis. You'll learn to analyze and understand behavior, develop effective interventions, and apply evidence-based strategies in various settings. The curriculum emphasizes practical application through supervised fieldwork, research opportunities, and hands-on experiences.
Accredidation: Our Verified Course Sequence (VCS) is approved by the Association for Behavior Analysis International (ABAI) and meets the coursework requirements for eligibility to take the Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) examination.

Requirements: Please make sure to have all of the following items ready for submission when you apply online: Three letters of recommendation, Official transcripts from all universities attended, Upload a statement of purpose outlining your research interests and career goals (approximately 1-2 pages), Upload a curriculum vitae (CV), Scores from the GRE General Test (optional for Fall 2024 admissions cycle and beyond), Scores from the TOEFL/IELTS (required for international students who did not complete their undergraduate or graduate degree at an institution where the sole language of instruction is English). The application deadline for the Ph.D. program in Psychology is December 1st.
Department: Graduate School of Arts and Science
Concentration: Cognition & Perception, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Neuroscience & Psychology
Description: The PhD in Psychology is an advanced research degree. The graduate program provides rigorous training in psychological science for students who wish to pursue careers in research and academia. The program emphasizes strong quantitative and methodological training, which students use to conduct original empirical research. Students learn to develop original ideas and test them empirically through coursework, seminars, and intensive research apprenticeships with faculty mentors. The program aims to foster the development of independent scholars who will make significant contributions to the field of psychological science. The typical time to degree is five years of full-time study. Most students are fully funded with a tuition waiver and stipends during their time in the program.

Requirements: Basic demographic information; Academic history (transcripts are not required, but you will be asked to list previously attended institutions and degrees earned/expected); Statement of Purpose; Resume/CV; Contact information for one professional or academic reference (letters of recommendation are not required, we will contact references by email if necessary)
Department: NYU Robert F. Wagner Graduate School of Public Service

Requirements: Online Application. A current professional resume or CV. A Statement of Purpose, no more than 500 words, that explains your motivation for pursuing an MPA degree at NYU Wagner. Your statement should describe how your professional, academic, and personal experiences have prepared you for graduate study in public service. Official academic transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended. Two letters of recommendation. Recommendations should be professional (i.e. from a supervisor or manager who can speak to your work experience) or academic (i.e. from a professor who can speak to your academic strengths). Family and friends should not write letters of recommendation. See more information on recommendations below. GRE/GMAT: Official test scores from the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) or the Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT) are optional. English Language Proficiency (if applicable): Applicants whose native language is not English and whose undergraduate degree was not taught in English must submit official English Language Proficiency test scores. Application Fee: $85 non-refundable application fee.
Department: NYU Robert F. Wagner Graduate School of Public Service
Concentration: Financial Management, International Development, Management & Leadership, Policy Analysis, Public Policy Analysis, Social Impact, Innovation, and Investment, Urban Planning
Description: The Master of Public Administration (MPA) at NYU Wagner is one of the nation’s top graduate professional degrees. It prepares students from a wide range of backgrounds to be leaders who can translate ideas into action and move society forward. Our flexible curriculum allows students to gain the analytical and management skills necessary to be effective public service leaders, while also specializing in a policy area or management function of their choosing. You’ll learn how to analyze and shape policy; manage people, projects, and organizations; and communicate effectively with stakeholders. Our graduates are equipped to lead mission-driven organizations in government, nonprofits, and the private sector, in New York City and around the world.

Requirements: Online Application, Resume or CV, Statement of Purpose, Official Transcripts, Two Letters of Recommendation, GRE Scores (Optional): While GRE scores are not a required component of the application, applicants may submit their scores if they feel they will strengthen their candidacy. English Language Proficiency: All applicants are required to demonstrate English language proficiency. If English is not your native language and you have not received a degree from an institution where the sole language of instruction is English, you must submit scores from the TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test.

Applicants for the Certificate in Public Health must complete the SOPH Supplemental Application and submit: Unofficial transcripts from all institutions of higher learning attended. Official transcripts will be required upon admission. A statement of purpose. A current resume or CV. Two letters of recommendation. Applicants must hold a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have maintained a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher from their undergraduate institution.
Description: The Public Health Certificate provides an introduction to the core functions of public health and population health. This 12-credit certificate provides students with foundational knowledge in the disciplines of epidemiology, biostatistics, environmental health, social and behavioral sciences, and health policy and management. The certificate is designed for students seeking to gain a basic understanding of public health principles or those who wish to enhance their professional skills in areas related to population health. The certificate is especially useful for clinicians, social workers, educators, and other professionals who work with diverse populations.
Accredidation: NYU Public Health is CEPH accredited.

Requirements: Applicants to the NYU School of Global Public Health’s MPH program must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must apply via the Schools of Public Health Application Service (SOPHAS) at sophas.org. Required Application Materials: Resume/CV, Statement of Purpose, GRE General Test (optional), Letters of Recommendation, Official Transcripts, English Language Proficiency (for international students).
Description: The NYU GPH Master of Public Health (MPH) is a 45-credit professional degree available in 10 concentrations that train students to be leaders in the public health field. Through a required core curriculum, students gain foundational knowledge of the principles and practice of public health, along with practical skills through hands-on experiences. Our graduates are prepared to address pressing public health challenges locally and globally in a variety of settings.
Accredidation: The NYU School of Global Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

Requirements: A complete application to the MPH program includes: Online Application, Academic History (transcripts), Statement of Purpose, Resume/Curriculum Vitae (CV), Letters of Recommendation (2), and Graduate Record Examination (GRE). The NYU School of Global Public Health has waived the GRE requirement for all Master of Public Health (MPH) applicants for the 2024-2025 application cycle. Submitting GRE scores is optional and scores will be considered if provided. If you choose to submit GRE scores, official scores must be sent directly from ETS to NYU GPH using institution code 5233. Scores are valid for five years.
Concentration: Applied Biostatistics, Community Health, Global Health
Description:
NYU GPH’s online Master of Public Health program brings the entire public health field to you. Designed to accommodate the needs of working professionals, the rigorous program is rooted in the school’s core values of research, education, and service, ensuring you will graduate with the skills to address pressing public health issues.

As an online MPH student, you will learn the core disciplines of public health, along with topics in epidemiology, biostatistics, environmental health, health policy, and social and behavioral sciences. Students also choose one of three concentrations – custom-designed for the online format: Applied Biostatistics, Community Health, or Global Health. Our online MPH delivers a diverse and engaging curriculum that builds on your career experiences and prepares you for leadership roles in various public health fields.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

Department: NYU School of Global Public Health
NYU School of Global Public Health
Description: Designed for students with a professional degree, strong research interests, or prior experience in the field of public health, the Master of Science in Public Health (MSPH) program at NYU’s School of Global Public Health provides advanced methodological, analytical, and data-driven skills needed for public health practice and research. The MSPH enables students to deepen their understanding of critical public health issues while developing the leadership and communication skills necessary to create positive change within complex health systems. With hands-on opportunities to apply theory to real-world challenges, students gain the tools to design, implement, and evaluate public health interventions.
