*   Letters of Recommendation (Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation)
*   Mid-Year Report (if applicable)
Description: Develop advanced proficiency in Spanish through rigorous linguistic, literary, and cultural studies. Gain a deep understanding of linguistic theories and methods, with a particular focus on the Spanish language. Analyze the structure and function of Spanish from phonetic, phonological, morphological, syntactic, and semantic perspectives. Explore the sociolinguistics of Spanish, including dialectal variation, language contact, and language attitudes. Critically engage with literary and cultural texts in Spanish, interpreting their linguistic and cultural significance. Conduct independent research in Spanish linguistics or literary/cultural studies, applying appropriate methodologies and theoretical frameworks. Communicate effectively in Spanish, both orally and in writing, demonstrating nuanced understanding of linguistic and cultural contexts.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish and Portuguese
Description: Students of the Spanish and Portuguese major acquire a deep understanding of the languages and cultures of the Spanish and Portuguese-speaking worlds. Through the interdisciplinary study of literature, film, visual arts, music, history, and current events, students hone their critical thinking and analytical skills. The major prepares students for graduate study, as well as for careers in education, diplomacy, international business, translation, law, and other fields that require advanced cross-cultural understanding and linguistic proficiency.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Urban Design and Architecture Studies
Requirements: Common Application or Coalition Application, Official High School Transcript(s), Mid-Year Report (if applicable), Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, Standardized Test Scores (Optional for Fall 2024), English Language Testing (if applicable), NYU Writing Supplement (short answer response to 'Why NYU? Why are you interested in studying at NYU?').
Description: The Urban Design and Architecture Studies major provides an interdisciplinary approach to the study of the city, its architectural and urban history, present form, and future design. Students learn to analyze cities through the lenses of history, theory, and design, drawing on a wide range of analytical and representational techniques. They develop skills in critical thinking, research, and communication, preparing them for careers in urban planning, architectural design, historic preservation, real estate, and public policy, as well as for graduate study in related fields. The curriculum includes courses in urban history, architectural history, design studios, and fieldwork opportunities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Urban Studies
Requirements: You must apply to NYU using either the Common Application or Coalition Application. Whichever application you choose, it will include: NYU-specific questions. Required for all applicants: Common Application or Coalition Application Essay, High School Transcript, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, Mid-Year Report, English Language Testing (if applicable). Standardized Testing is optional for Fall 2024, 2025, and 2026 applicants.
Description: Urban Studies and History is an interdisciplinary major offered jointly by the Department of History and the Gallatin School of Individualized Study. This major explores the history and development of cities, their social, economic, political, and cultural formations, and their representation in various forms of media.

ProgramName: Associate in Applied Science in Dental Hygiene
Requirements:
Admission to the NYU Dental Hygiene Program is highly selective. We encourage prospective students to gain a comprehensive understanding of the profession prior to applying. The following minimum requirements apply to all applicants:
1. Academic Requirements: High school diploma or GED/TASC certificate is required. Minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 (on a 4.0 scale) from all previously attended colleges/universities. Minimum science GPA of 2.5 (on a 4.0 scale) for all biology and chemistry courses. All prerequisite science courses must have been completed within five years prior to the application date and with a grade of "C" or better. Prerequisite courses include: English Composition I and II (6 credits), Introduction to Psychology (3 credits), Introduction to Sociology (3 credits), General Biology I with lab (4 credits), General Biology II with lab (4 credits), General Chemistry I with lab (4 credits), Introduction to Organic Chemistry with lab (4 credits) (or combined Organic/Biochemistry), Introduction to Biochemistry with lab (4 credits) (or combined Organic/Biochemistry), Anatomy and Physiology I with lab (4 credits), Anatomy and Physiology II with lab (4 credits), Microbiology with lab (4 credits), Nutrition (3 credits), Statistics (3 credits). All prerequisite science courses for the AAS program MUST be taken for science majors. NYU does not accept AP/IB credits for science courses.
2. English Language Proficiency: If English is not your native language and you have not received a degree from an institution where English is the primary language of instruction, you must submit official scores for one of the following exams: TOEFL iBT (minimum score of 85), IELTS Academic (minimum score of 6.5 overall band score), Duolingo English Test (minimum score of 115), PTE Academic (minimum score of 57). Scores must be valid within two years of application.
3. Computer Literacy: Familiarity with common computer applications (e.g., word processing, email, internet).
4. Technical Standards for Admission and Retention: Applicants must meet specific physical, cognitive, and behavioral abilities required for the profession (refer to the Technical Standards for Admission and Retention document for details).
5. CPR Certification: Current CPR certification (BLS for Healthcare Providers by American Heart Association, or Professional Rescuer by American Red Cross) is required prior to beginning the program.
Applications for admission to the AAS Program are submitted via ADEA DHCAS (Dental Hygiene Centralized Application Service). The DHCAS application requires the following: Official Transcripts from all colleges/universities attended, Two Letters of Recommendation (one from a science professor and one from a supervisor or employer (non-relative)), a Personal Statement (a one-page essay describing your motivations for pursuing a career in dental hygiene and choosing NYU), and Verification of 20 hours of observation in a dental setting (general or specialty practice) with a licensed dentist or registered dental hygienist.
Description: As a dental hygienist, you’re an integral member of the dental care team. The dental hygienist provides clinical, educational, and therapeutic services that help people maintain optimal oral health. The Associate in Applied Science (AAS) in Dental Hygiene program at NYU College of Dentistry prepares you to deliver these services in a variety of health care settings.
Accredidation: The dental hygiene program is accredited by the Commission on Dental Accreditation (CODA) of the American Dental Association (ADA).
